newsitem.title: USA: Conn. governor vows arena to stay in Hartford.
newsitem.headline: Conn. governor vows arena to stay in Hartford.

text.p: Governor John Rowland will not support any plans to build a new arena for the National Hockey League's Hartford Whalers outside of the capital city, his press secretary said Friday.
The Whalers have said the state must build a new arena, costing as much as $240 million in taxpayers' money, if it wants the team to stay in Connecticut.
Rowland's Press Secretary Dean Pagani told Reuters the governor is against taking the Whalers out of Hartford.

Rowland will meet with Whalers owner Peter Karmanos on January 9 to discuss several options that could keep the hockey team in Hartford, said Pagani. It will be the pair's first discussion in more than three months.

The options include spending an estimated $10-12 million to refurbish the Hartford Civic Center, or possibly building a new arena in Hartford if the Whalers agree to stay in the city for at least 15 years, said Pagani.
The team's owner was quoted in the Hartford Courant on Friday as saying that Rowland had not yet shared the state's ideas with him.
"I just hope it's not politics as usual - that he's not just making sure to say nice things in the newspaper," said Karmanos.
Pagani said next week's meeting was the governor's idea and that Rowland was serious.

"The Whalers are pretty high up on his priorities," said Pagani. "The legislature is about to open its session, and he's working on his budget... But the Whalers issue takes a high profile, because they're such a public enterprise."
